samples.summary: The frontend's own `treeNodeToBlock` clamp (the real collaborative read boundary the app uses) has no test for a poisoned `listLevel`
samples.evidence: The diff adds `normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))` to packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:496. The engine copy in packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts is covered by test/model/list-level.test.ts:212 ('the CRDT read boundary clamps a peer-supplied level'), but the frontend duplicate is not: grepping `listLevel` in packages/frontend/tests only finds pre-existing round-trip tests with levels 0/1 (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1587,1935,2375,2425,2460) and none feeding `Infinity`, `1e9`, `-4` or a non-numeric attribute. This is the copy that actually runs in the product, and frontend has no `tsc` lane, so a regression here (the guard being dropped or the argument order changed) would ship silently and let a hostile/garbled peer attribute blank the rendered document via `levelCounters.length = NaN` / `'  '.repeat(2e9)`.

samples.summary: `Doc.siblingBlocksOf` / `walkCellsForSiblings` have no direct unit test; the nested-table recursion, footer region and not-found branches are unexercised
samples.evidence: grep for `siblingBlocksOf` finds only src usages plus a task doc — no test file references it, and packages/docs/test/model/document.test.ts has no such describe. It is exercised only indirectly through editor-tab-bullet.test.ts ('a cell caret missing from the parent map still carries its subtree', 'Cmd+] survives a parent map pointing at a table that is gone'), both of which use a single top-level table in the body. The recursive `walkCellsForSiblings` descent into a *nested* table cell, the header/footer cell fallback (only header *top-level* blocks are covered, by the 'a header list carries its children too' test), and the `undefined` return for a block absent from the document are all untested. A regression there degrades a Tab/Cmd+] gesture into a silent no-op — contained, but user-visible.

samples.summary: The two new `normalizeListLevel` calls in the PDF painter are untested
samples.evidence: pdf-painter.ts:370 and :593 now normalize the level before it is multiplied into the marker x and used as a `listCounters` map key, but grep for `listLevel` in packages/docs/test/export/pdf-painter.test.ts returns 0 matches, and pdf-exporter.test.ts's list coverage (line 333, 'exports list items with markers') uses the with-list.json fixture with ordinary levels and a variant where listLevel is set to `undefined`. No test exports a document with a NaN/1e9 level, so nothing would catch the clamp being removed and NaN coordinates reaching pdf-lib.

samples.summary: The paint/marker/caret normalizations (paint-layout, doc-canvas, table-renderer, peer-cursor) have no poisoned-level test
samples.evidence: list-level.test.ts covers the raw readers only for `computeListCounters`, `computeTableLayout` and the markdown serializer (test/model/list-level.test.ts:227-275). The equally-new clamps in paint-layout.ts:199, doc-canvas.ts:600, table-renderer.ts:529 and peer-cursor.ts:255/395 — each of which turns a poisoned level into a NaN marker or caret x (an invisible caret / marker) — are not asserted anywhere: the existing paint-layout.test.ts, render-list-marker.test.ts, table-renderer.test.ts and peer-cursor.test.ts use ordinary levels (grep `listLevel` shows no NaN/Infinity/1e9 cases). Failure is a silently missing caret or bullet rather than a crash, so contained, but nothing guards these five call sites.
searchedFor: grep NaN/Infinity in docs view tests

samples.summary: The text-box editor's new `doc.batch()` wrapping (the 'one undo unit' contract) is never asserted
samples.evidence: The docs editor's batching is directly observed by the `TracingStore` in editor-tab-bullet.test.ts (`expect(store.writeDepths).toEqual([1, 1])`, plus a one-undo-restores-the-subtree test). The text-box equivalent added at text-box-editor.ts:1165-1200 has only the new test in test/view/text-box-editor.test.ts:551 ('indent / outdent carry a list item's nested children'), which asserts the committed levels via `onCommit` and says nothing about batching or undo. If the `doc.batch()` wrapper were dropped there, that test still passes while a single Cmd+Z leaves the subtree half-moved in Slides/Board.
searchedFor: read the text-box-editor test hunk in the diff

samples.summary: The carried-child repaint (`markDirty`) is only proven for top-level blocks, not for a child inside a table cell
samples.evidence: The new 'a carried child repaints at its new depth' describe (editor-tab-bullet.test.ts) exercises only body top-level items, where `markDirty(cellInfo?.tableBlockId ?? change.block.id)` falls through to the block's own id. The table-cell path — where the dirty id must come from `doc.blockParentMap` and where the surrounding tests deliberately delete/poison that map entry — is asserted only at the model level (`cellLevels(store)`), never via painted x. So a carried child in a cell repainting at its old indent (the exact failure the markDirty line exists to prevent, and which a stale/missing parent-map entry can still produce) would not be caught.
searchedFor: read the 'a carried child repaints at its new depth' describe in the diff

finding.summary: The frontend's own `treeNodeToBlock` clamp (the real collaborative read boundary the app uses) has no test for a poisoned `listLevel`
finding.evidence: The diff adds `normalizeListLevel(Number(attrs.listLevel))` to packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:496. The engine copy in packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts is covered by test/model/list-level.test.ts:212 ('the CRDT read boundary clamps a peer-supplied level'), but the frontend duplicate is not: grepping `listLevel` in packages/frontend/tests only finds pre-existing round-trip tests with levels 0/1 (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:1587,1935,2375,2425,2460) and none feeding `Infinity`, `1e9`, `-4` or a non-numeric attribute. verdict.reason: The literal absence is real — no frontend test feeds a poisoned listLevel through packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:501 (the poisoned-attribute suite at yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2637-2699 covers lineHeight/marginTop/textIndent/marginFromEdge only) — but it is not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric. The frontend line has no logic of its own: it is a unary call into the shared normalizeListLevel, which is exhaustively unit-tested (list-level.test.ts:174-198) and whose identical Number(attrs.listLevel) string-coercion boundary is tested with '1e9'/'Infinity'/'not-a-number'/'-4' (list-level.test.ts:212-225). Both crash sinks the finding names as the user-visible impact are independently clamped and covered: levelCounters.length = NaN at layout.ts:1097 (test at list-level.test.ts:227-242) and '  '.repeat(2e9) at markdown.ts:145 (test at list-level.test.ts:266-275), with the same defense at table-layout.ts:97, doc-canvas.ts:603, paint-layout.ts:200, table-renderer.ts:529, peer-cursor.ts:257,396 and pdf-painter.ts:370,593. The frontend's reliance on the helper is further protected by the entry-parity test (entry-parity.test.ts:41-56), added precisely because normalizeListLevel once shipped on the browser entry alone and broke the frontend integration suites. The reviewer's 'argument order changed' regression is inapplicable to a one-argument function. So dropping the frontend clamp could not blank or crash the rendered document undetected; the gap is contained coverage narrowness (minor), which this lens defers rather than gates on.
